Then they departed from Ibrahim, heading toward the people of Lut, and the distance between the village of Ibrahim and the people of Lut was four farsakh (parasangs)."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 77:

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed on their account and felt helpless for them﴾ They came to him, and he saw their forms and their beauty, ﴿and he was distressed on their account﴾, meaning he was saddened, because he thought they were humans and feared for them the wickedness of his people, and that he would be unable to resist and repel them. ﴿And he felt constrained for them﴾ (tamyiz, i.e., the accusative of specification): that is, his breast was constricted by their presence. ﴿And he said, "This is a distressing day."﴾ That is, severe.

It is narrated that God the Exalted said to them, "Do not destroy them until Lut testifies against them four times." So when he walked with them, leading them to his home, he said to them, "Has not the news of this town reached you?" They said, "And what is their affair?" He said, "I bear witness by God that it is the worst town on earth in its deeds," and he said this four times. They then entered his house with him, and no one knew of that. Then his wife went out and informed her people about them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 78:

﴿And his people came to him, hastening towards him.﴾ They were hastening, as if they were being pushed forcibly. ﴿And before this they used to do evil deeds.﴾ That is, before that time they used to commit abominations, until they became accustomed to them, and their sense of their ugliness diminished. Therefore they came hastening towards him, openly, with no shame restraining them. ﴿He said: "O my people, these are my daughters."﴾ So marry them. He intended to shield his guests with his daughters, and that is the utmost of generosity. Marrying Muslim women to disbelievers was permissible at that time, just as it was permissible at the beginning of this community. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married his two daughters to ʿUtbah ibn Abi Lahab and Abu al-ʿAs, and both were disbelievers. It is said that they had two obeyed leaders, so Lut wanted to marry them to his daughters. ﴿They are purer for you﴾: more lawful. "Hā'ulā'" is the subject (mubtada'), "banātī" is an appositive (ʿaṭf bayān), and "hunna" is a separator (faṣl), and "aṭhar" is the predicate of the subject. Or "banātī" is the predicate, and "hunna aṭhar" is a subject and predicate. ﴿So fear Allah﴾ by preferring them over him. ﴿And do not disgrace me﴾: do not humiliate me, nor expose me to shame, from "khizy" (disgrace), or do not embarrass me, from "khizāya," which is shame. With a yāʾ (reading "tukhzūnī" with yāʾ in connected speech) is Abu ʿAmr. ﴿Concerning my guests﴾: regarding my guests. For when a man's guest or neighbor is disgraced, the man himself is disgraced, and that is from the nobility of generosity and the authenticity of manliness. ﴿Is there not among you a man of sound judgment?﴾ That is: one man who is guided to the path of truth, to doing what is good, and to refraining from evil.

﴿They said: You certainly know that we have no right to your daughters﴾. *Ḥājah* (need): meaning, we have no need of them, because marrying females is a matter outside our *madhhab* (way, practice), and our *madhhab* is *ityān al-dhukrān* (approaching males). ﴿And indeed you know what we desire﴾. They meant *ityān al-dhukūr* (approaching males) and the desire they have for it. (p-76)

﴿He said: "If only I had power against you, or could take refuge in a strong support."﴾ The answer to *law* (the conditional particle "if") is omitted, meaning: "I would have done to you, and I would have acted." The meaning is: "If I were strong against you myself, or if I had taken refuge with a powerful one to lean on, by whom I could protect myself and who would shield me from you." He likened the mighty, powerful one to a *rukn* (support, pillar) of a mountain in its firmness and its ability to protect. It is narrated that he closed his door when they came, and began turning them away, as God related of him, and arguing with them. So they climbed over the wall. When the angels saw what Lut suffered of distress,

﴿They said, "O Lut!"﴾ Indeed, your *rukn* (support, kin, and protectors) is strong. ﴿Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord.﴾ So open the door and leave us and them alone. He opened the door, and they entered. Jibril (Gabriel), upon him be peace, asked his Lord for permission to punish them, and He granted it. He struck their faces with his wing, obliterating their eyes and blinding them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We obliterated their eyes﴾ [al-Qamar 54:37]. They then could not find the way. They went out saying, "Rescue!" "Indeed, in the house of Lut there are sorcerers." ﴿They will not reach you﴾ is a sentence clarifying the one before it, because if they were the messengers of Allah, they could not reach him and could not harm him.

﴿So travel﴾ with wasl (connected vowel) is the reading of the Hijazi (Ibn Kathir), from *sara*. ﴿with your family in a portion of the night﴾, meaning a part of it or half of it. ﴿And let none of you look back﴾, meaning with his heart toward what he left behind, or: let none of you look at what is behind him, or: let none of you fall behind. ﴿Except your wife﴾ is an exception from "﴿So travel with your family﴾". Reading it with *raf'* (nominative, *imra'atuka*) is the reading of Makki (Ibn Kathir) and Abu 'Amr, as a *badal* (substitute) from "*ahad*" (anyone). Regarding her going out with his family there are two reports. It is narrated that he took her out with them and commanded that none of them look back except her; when she heard the thunder of the punishment, she looked back and said, "O my people!" A stone then caught her and killed her. It is also narrated that he was commanded to leave her behind with her people, since her inclination was toward them, so he did not travel with her. The difference between the two readings corresponds to the difference between the two reports. ﴿Indeed, it will befall her what befalls them﴾, meaning: indeed, the matter is so. It is narrated that he said to them, "When is the appointed time of their destruction?" They said, ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning﴾. He said (p-77), "I want it sooner than that." They said, ﴿Is not the morning near?﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 82:

﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest, and rained down upon it stones of sijjil, layered one upon another﴾ Jibril (peace be upon him) placed his wing beneath it, that is, beneath its lowest part (asfal qura-ha), then lifted it up to the sky until the people of the sky heard the barking of dogs and the crowing of roosters. Then he overturned it upon them, and they were pursued by stones from above them. This is His saying: ﴿And We rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾. Sijjil is a word that has been arabized (mu'arrabah) from "sang-i gil" (Persian), as is shown by His saying "stones of clay" (hijaratan min tin). ﴿Mandud﴾ is an attribute (na't) of sijjil, that is, consecutive (mutata'bi') or gathered and prepared (mujtama' mu'edd) for the punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 83:

﴿Marked﴾ is an attribute of "stones," meaning: marked for the punishment. It was said: on each one was written the name of the person it would be hurled at. ﴿With your Lord﴾ — in His treasuries, or in His decree. ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ — it is not far at all. In this there is a warning to the people of Makkah, for Jibril (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning the wrongdoers of your community: there is no wrongdoer among them but he is at the distance of a stone's throw, which falls at any moment from one hour to another. Or the pronoun refers to the towns: that is, they are near the wrongdoers of Makkah, who pass by them on their journeys.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 84:

﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb.﴾ This is either the name of their city or the name of their forefather Madyan ibn Ibrahim (Madyan ibn Ibrahim). That is: We sent Shu'ayb to the inhabitants of Madyan, or to the children of Madyan. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure (al-mikyal)﴾ meaning, what is measured by the measure, ﴿and the scale (al-mizan)﴾ and what is weighed by the scale. ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity (bi-khayr)﴾ in wealth and abundance that should suffice you from cheating (al-taṭfif), or: I see you in a blessing from Allah, which deserves to be met with other than what you are doing. ﴿And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a encompassing day﴾ destroying, from His saying, "and its fruit was encompassed (wa-uhīṭa bi-thamarihi)" [Q. 18:42]. Its root is from the encompassing (ihata) of an enemy. The intended meaning is the punishment of total annihilation in this world, or the punishment of the Hereafter. (p-78)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 85:

﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight﴾ — complete them ﴿with justice﴾, that is, with equity. They were first forbidden the very ugliness they were engaged in, namely the shortchanging of measure and weight; then the command to give full measure came, which is good by the standard of reason, to increase the encouragement toward it. It was brought qualified by "with justice," meaning: let the giving of full measure be in the manner of fairness and equality, without excess or deficiency. ﴿And do not diminish for people their things﴾ — al-bakhs (بَخْس) is deficiency. They used to shortchange on the prices of the goods they bought, so they were forbidden from that. ﴿And do not commit abuse in the earth, causing corruption﴾ — al-'uthiyy (عُثِيّ) and al-'ayth (عَيْث) are the most severe corruption, such as theft, raiding, and cutting off the road. It is also permissible to make the diminishing and the shortchanging a form of 'ayth (عَيْث) committed by them upon the earth.

"Allah's remainder (baqiyyat Allah) is better for you, if you are believers" (﴿بَقِيَّتُ اللهِ﴾ ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾). That is: what remains for you of the lawful (ḥalāl) after abstaining from what is forbidden to you. "If you are believers": on the condition that you believe. Yes, Allah's remainder is also better for the disbelievers, because with it they are safe from the consequence of defrauding and cheating (al-bakhs wa-al-taṭfīf). However, its benefit appears fully with faith, in obtaining reward together with salvation from punishment, and it also appears without faith, since its possessor is immersed in the depths of disbelief. In this there is a magnification of faith and an alert to the greatness of its status. Or the meaning is: "if you are those who affirm me in what I tell you and what I advise you with."

﴿وَما أنا عَلَيْكم بِحَفِيظٍ﴾ "And I am not a guardian over you": over His blessings upon you, so guard them by abandoning defrauding.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 87:

﴿They said: "O Shu'ayb! Does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we should not do with our wealth what we please?"﴾ Among the readers, Kufans other than Abu Bakr read "بِالتَوْحِيدِ" (bi-al-tawhid, with the doubled letter) [the Arabic words are a reading note on the verb's pronunciation]. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, used to pray very much, and his people would say to him: "What benefit do you gain from this?" He would say: "Indeed, it commands what is good and forbids what is evil." So they said, mockingly: "Does your prayer command you," [meaning] that it should command you to abandon worshipping what our fathers worshipped, or that we should not extravagantly spend our wealth as we please, through giving in full or diminishing [the measure]. It is permissible for the prayers to be described as "commanding" figuratively, just as Allah the Exalted named them "forbidding" figuratively. ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾, i.e., the foolish, the misguided. This is a designation by inversion, as mockery; or [it means]: "Indeed, you are forbearing and rightly guided in our view, and you do not do to us what your condition requires."

He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me from Himself a good provision" (﴿مِن لَدُنْهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا﴾), meaning prophethood and messagehood, or lawful wealth without defrauding or short-measuring. The answer to "tell me" (ara'aytum) is omitted, meaning: inform me, if I am upon a manifest proof from my Lord and I am truly a prophet, is it right for me not to command you to abandon the worship of idols and to refrain from sins? Prophets are sent only for that.

It is said: "Fulan opposed me toward such-and-such" (khalafani ila kadha) when he intends it while you turn away from it. And "he opposed me from it" (khalafani 'anhu) when he turns away from it while you intend it. A man may meet you coming back from the water, and you ask him about his companion, and he says: "He opposed me toward the water" (khalafani ila al-ma'), meaning that he has gone to it and intended it while I am going away from it, returning.

From this is His saying: ﴿وَما أُرِيدُ أنْ أُخالِفَكم إلى ما أنْهاكم عَنْهُ﴾ ("And I do not want to oppose you by doing what I forbid you from"), meaning: I do not want to get ahead of you to the desires that I have forbidden you, so as to monopolize them without you. ﴿إنْ أُرِيدُ إلا الإصْلاحَ﴾ ("I want nothing but reform"), meaning: I want only to reform you through my admonition, my counsel, my commanding of what is right, and my forbidding of what is wrong. ﴿ما اسْتَطَعْتُ﴾ ("as far as I am able") is an adverbial of time (zarf), meaning: for the duration of my ability to reform, and as long as I am able to do so, I spare no effort in it. ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللهِ﴾ ("And my success is only through Allah"), meaning: my being granted success in hitting the truth in what I do and what I leave undone is only through His help and support. ﴿عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ ("In Him I have put my trust"), meaning: I relied upon Him. ﴿وَإلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ﴾ ("And to Him I turn back"), meaning: I return to Him in ease and in hardship.

Jarama is like kasaba, whether it takes one object or two. From this is His saying: ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you [the like of] what afflicted the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih﴾, meaning: let not my opposition earn for you the affliction of punishment ﴿like what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih﴾, namely drowning, the wind, and the earthquake. ﴿And the people of Lot are not far from you﴾ in time, so they are the nearest of the destroyed to you; or in place, so their dwellings are near to you; or in what deserves destruction, namely disbelief and evil deeds. The word "qarib" (near), "ba'id" (far), "qalil" (few) and "kathir" (many) is used equally for the masculine and the feminine, because they occur in the pattern of verbal nouns (masadir) such as "sahil" (neighing) and "nahiq" (braying) and similar words.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 90:

﴿And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful, Affectionate﴾ — He forgives the people of harshness (jafa') among the believers. ﴿Affectionate (wadud)﴾ — He loves the people of fidelity (wafa') among the righteous.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 91:

﴿They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say."﴾ That is: we do not comprehend the soundness of what you say. Otherwise, how could his speech not be understood, when he is the orator of the prophets (khatib al-anbiya')?  ﴿And indeed, we see you as weak among us.﴾ You have no strength and no might among us, so you cannot prevent us from you if we intend you some harm. ﴿And were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you.﴾ Had it not been for your kinsmen, we would have killed you by stoning, which is the worst kind of killing. His clan (rahtuhu) were among the people of his religion, and therefore they showed inclination toward them and honor for them. ﴿And you are not esteemed by us.﴾ That is: you are not held in honor by us, nor are you respected so that we would honor you by sparing you from killing and lifting from you stoning. Rather, your clan are esteemed by us, because they are of our religion. The placement of his pronoun after the negative particle (ma) indicates that the speech concerns the agent and not the act, as if it were said: "And you are not esteemed by us; rather, your clan are the ones esteemed by us."

He said, in reply to them: "O my people, is my tribe more honoured by you than God?" If it were said, "You have not been held in esteem by us," this answer would not be valid. Rather, he said, "Is my tribe more honoured by you than God?" The speech is directed at him and at his tribe, and that they are the ones held in honour by them rather than him. For their contempt for him, while he is the Prophet of God, is contempt for God. And when his tribe was held in greater honour by them than he was, his tribe was more honoured by them than God. Do you not see the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed God﴾ [al-Nisa': 80]?

﴿And you have taken Him behind your backs﴾: you have forgotten Him and made Him like a thing cast behind the back, not regarded at all. The word ẓihriyy (ظِهْرِيًّا, "behind the back") is a relative form derived from ẓahr (ظهر, "back"), and the kasra (vowel i) is one of the alterations of the relative form, like their saying in the relative form of amsi (الأمس, "yesterday") as imsiyy (إمسيّ).

﴿Indeed my Lord is encompassing of what you do﴾: He has encompassed your deeds with knowledge, so nothing of them is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 93:

﴿And O my people, act according to your standing﴾. It means "place" (makan). One says makan, makana, maqam and maqama. Or it is a verbal noun (masdar) from makuna (makan), so one is makin (makin) when one is firmly established in something. That is, act while steadfast upon your way in which you are, of polytheism and enmity towards me; or act firmly established in your hostility towards me, fully committed to it. ﴿Indeed I am acting﴾ according to what Allah grants me of help and support and enables me to do. ﴿You will soon know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him, and who is a liar﴾. "Man" (من) here is an interrogative (istifhamiyyah) suspending the verb of knowledge ('ilm) from its action in it, as if it were said: "You will soon know which of us will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and which of us is a liar." Or it is a relative pronoun (mawsulah) whose government the verb has taken, as if it were said: "You will soon know the wretched one who will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and the one who is a liar in your claim and your assertion." Inserting the fa' (ف) before "sawfa" (سوف) is an apparent connection (wasl zahir) by a particle set for connection, and omitting it is an implied connection (wasl taqdiri) by resumption (isti'naf), which is an answer to an implied question, as if they had said: "So what will happen if we act upon our standing and you act?" Then he said: "You will soon know." Bringing both forms is for variety in eloquence, and the more eloquent of the two is the resumption (istinaf). ﴿And watch﴾, and await the outcome and what I say to you. ﴿Indeed I am with you a watcher (raqib)﴾, awaiting. Raqib is in the sense of rakib (one who watches), from raqabahu, like darib (striker) in the sense of darib (one who strikes); or in the sense of murāqib (one who observes), like 'ashir (companion) in the sense of mu'ashir (one who associates); or in the sense of murtaqib (one who awaits), like rafi' (elevated) in the sense of murtafi' (one who is elevated).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 94:

﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the Cry seized those who had wronged, so they lay prostrate in their homes by morning.﴾ Jibril (Gabriel) cried out at them, and they perished. And the reason that "and when" (wa-lamma jā'a) is mentioned at the end of the story of ʿĀd and Madyan, while "then when" (fa-lamma jā'a) is mentioned at the end of the story of Thamud and Lot, is that the former two came after the mention of the appointed time, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning﴾. That is a promise not to be denied. So the particle fa- (which indicates causation) was used, as when you say: "I promised him, and when the appointment came, such-and-such happened." As for the other two, they came as independent beginnings, so their right was to be joined by the conjunctive particle to what precedes them, just as one story is joined to another story. ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate.﴾ Al-jāthim is one who remains fixed in his place and does not move. The meaning is that Jibril cried at them a single cry, so the soul of each one of them departed suddenly where he was.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 95:

﴿As though they had never dwelt therein.﴾ As though they had never inhabited their dwellings, living and going about and coming and going. ﴿Ah, away with Madyan!﴾ The word bu'd (بُعْد) here has the sense of ba'ad (بَعَد), which is destruction, just as rushd (رُشْد) has the sense of rashad (رَشَد). Do you not see His saying ﴿as Thamud were destroyed﴾? It is also read "kama ba'udat" (كَما بَعُدَتْ). The meaning in both patterns is one, and it is the opposite of nearness, except that they differentiated between "bu'd" in the sense of destruction and other than it, so they changed the pattern, just as they differentiated between the two transitive forms of good and evil, so they said wa'ada (وَعَدَ) and aw'ada (أوْعَدَ).
And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs and a manifest authority (﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا وسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾). What is meant by it is the staff, because it overwhelmed them.

To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guided. (The chiefs are meant by "al-mala'".) The phrase "and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guided" is a condemnation of his followers (tajhil), in that they followed him in his command, and that is manifest error. The reason is that he claimed divinity while he was a human being like them, prone to injustice and evil, which come only from Satan, and one like him is far removed from divinity. It also implies that they witnessed the signs and the clear authority, and knew that with Musa were right guidance and truth, yet they turned away from following him to following one in whose command there was never any guidance at all. Or the meaning is: his command was not conducive to a good and praiseworthy outcome; and his saying...

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 98:

﴿He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., he will lead them while they follow in his footsteps, as an explanation and clarification of it. That is: how can the affair of one whose end is such be rightly guided? Rushd (rectitude, right guidance) is used for everything that is praised and approved, just as ghayy (error) is used for everything that is blameworthy. It is also said: qadamahu means taqaddamahu (he went before him). ﴿And he will lead them into the Fire﴾, i.e., he will cause them to enter it. The past tense (fa-awradahum) is used here because the past tense indicates a matter that exists and is certain. It is as if it were said: he will go before them, and he will certainly bring them down into the Fire, meaning: just as he was a model for them in misguidance, so too he will go before them to the Fire while they follow him. ﴿And wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾. Al-warad is the place of watering, and al-mawrud is that to which one comes down (for water). He (the leader) is likened to the forerunner who goes ahead of the water-seekers to the water, and his followers are likened to those who come to the water. Then he says: "And wretched is the watering-place (al-warad) to which they are brought (al-mawrud)," meaning: the Fire, because the watering-place is only intended for quenching thirst, and the Fire is its opposite.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 99:

﴿And they were followed in this﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., they are cursed in this world and they are cursed in the Hereafter. ﴿Wretched is the gift that is given﴾, their gift, i.e., wretched is the help that is helped, or wretched is the gift that is given.

Translation:

﴿That﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), ﴿of the reports of the towns﴾ is the predicate (khabar). ﴿We relate it to you﴾ is a second predicate after a predicate (khabar ba'da khabar), meaning: that account is part of the reports of the destroyed towns, related to you. ﴿Of them﴾, of the towns, ﴿some are standing and some are reaped﴾, meaning: some of them remain, and some of them have had their traces effaced, like a crop standing upon its stalk and one that has been harvested. And the sentence is resumed (mustanba'afah), having no place in terms of i'rab.

﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by destroying them, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ by committing that for which they were destroyed. ﴿Then their gods, whom they called upon besides Allah, did not avail them at all﴾ — they were not able to ward off from them the punishment of Allah ﴿that they called upon besides Allah, of anything, when the command of your Lord came﴾ — His punishment. Lammā (when) is in the accusative governed by "did not avail" (mā aghnat). ﴿And they added nothing to them but ruin﴾ — tatbīb (perdition, loss). It is said: tabba (he perished) when he suffered loss, and tabbabahu (he caused him ruin) when another caused him to fall into loss. The meaning is: the worship of other than Allah profited them nothing; rather, it destroyed them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 102:

﴿And thus﴾ The place of the kaf (ka, "like") is in the nominative case, i.e., "and like that seizure is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns﴾, i.e., their people, ﴿while they are wrongdoers﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the towns. ﴿Indeed His seizure is painful, severe﴾: painful, severe, and difficult for the one seized. This is a warning to every wrongdoing town, among the disbelievers of Makkah and others, so every wrongdoer must hasten to repentance and not be deceived by the respite. (p-84)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 103:

﴿Indeed in that﴾ — that is, in what Allah has related of the stories of the destroyed nations — ﴿is a sign﴾, a lesson ('ibrah) ﴿for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter﴾, that is, who believe in its truth and its existence. ﴿That﴾ refers to the Day of Resurrection, because the punishment of the Hereafter points to it. ﴿It is a Day for which mankind will be gathered﴾ — it is in the nominative case by "majmu'" (gathered), just as its verb would raise it if you said: "mankind will be gathered for it" (yujma'u lahu al-nas). The author chose the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) over its verb because the passive participle indicates the permanence of the meaning of gathering for the Day, and it is also more firmly established regarding the attribution of gathering to mankind, and that they are not free of it: they are gathered for the reckoning, the reward and the punishment. ﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾ — that is, witnessed in it, so the adverb of time was broadened by treating it as the object (maf'ul bihi), meaning: the creatures witness the standing-place in it, and none will be absent from it.

ﷻ "And We do not delay it" — that is, the Day mentioned.

Al-ajal (the term, the appointed time): it is applied both to the whole duration of the postponement and to its end. Counting, however, belongs only to the duration, not to its limit and end. So the meaning of His words "And We do not delay it ﴿except for a countable term﴾" is: except until a counted period comes to its end, with the omission of a modifier (al-mudaf, the governed noun), or: We do not delay this Day except so that the period We set for the duration of the world may come to its end.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 105:

﴿On the day it comes﴾. Read with the yā' (يَأْتِ with yā') by Makki, and agreed with by Abu 'Amr, Nafi' and 'Ali in continuous recitation (waṣl). Retaining the yā' is the original form, since there is no cause that requires its deletion. Deleting the yā' and substituting the kasra for it (al-ijtizā' 'anhā bil-kasra) is common in the dialect of Hudhayl, and its parallel is ﴿مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ﴾ [al-Kahf: 64]. The subject of yaʾtī is a pronoun referring to the phrase "a day for which the people are gathered" (yawmun majmū'un lahu al-nās), not the day itself, which is the noun governed by yaʾtī. "Yawma" (on the day) is in the accusative, governed either by "udhkur" (remember) or by the words ﴿لا تَكَلَّمُ﴾ (no one speaks), meaning: ﴿لا تَتَكَلَّمُ﴾ (no soul speaks), ﴿نَفْسٌ إلا بِإذْنِهِ﴾ (except by His permission), meaning: no one intercedes except by the permission of God, as in "Who is it that intercedes with Him except by His permission?" ﴿فَمِنهُمْ﴾ (then among them): the pronoun refers to the people of the standing-place, because of the indication of "no soul speaks" toward it, and the mention of "people" has already passed in His words ﴿مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ الناسُ﴾ [Hud: 103]. ﴿شَقِيٌّ﴾ (wretched): tormented. ﴿وَسَعِيدٌ﴾ (and happy): i.e., and among them is one who is happy, meaning enjoying bliss.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 106:

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, where for them will be groaning and wailing.﴾ It is the first part of the braying of the donkey, ﴿and wailing﴾ is its last part; or they are the expelling of breath and its return. The clause is in the position of a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and the governing element (ʿāmil) in it is the settledness (istiqrār) that is in the Fire. (p-85)

﴿Abiding therein﴾ is a conditioned state (ḥāl muqaddara). ﴿As long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ is in the accusative position, meaning: for the duration of the enduring of the heavens and the earth. What is meant is the heavens and earth of the Hereafter, which are lasting and created for eternity. The evidence that they have heavens and earth is His saying: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens [as well]﴾ [Ibrahim: 48]. It has also been said that "as long as" means "as long as there is above and below." And because the people of the Hereafter must have something that carries them and shades them, whether a heaven or a throne, and everything that shades you is a heaven, or it is an expression for perpetuity and the negation of cessation, like the Arabs' saying: "No star has risen" (ma lāḥa kawkab), and other expressions of perpetuity.

﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾ is an exception from the eternity in the punishment of the Fire. This is because the people of the Fire are not made to abide only in the punishment of the Fire; rather they are punished with the zamharir (intense cold) and kinds of punishment other than the punishment of the Fire. Or "what" (mā shā'a) means "whoever" (man shā'a), referring to a people who will come out of the Fire and enter the Garden; they are called the Jahannamiyyun (the people of Hell), and they are also excluded from the people of the Garden, because they have parted from it by having been in the Fire for a period. These people have not suffered the wretchedness of those who enter the Fire forever, nor have they attained the felicity of those whom the Fire does not touch. This is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḍaḥḥak and Qatada, may Allah be pleased with them. ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Doer of what He intends﴾ regarding the wretched and the happy.

And as for those who were made happy (suʿidu): Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and Ḥafs read "suʿidū" (passive). saʿida is intransitive, while saʿadahu yasʿadahu is transitive. ﴿Then in the Garden they will abide therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾. This is an exception from the abiding in the bliss of the Garden. That is because they have, beyond the Garden, something greater than it, namely the vision of God, the Exalted, and His good pleasure. Or its meaning is: except for the one whom He wills to punish in proportion to his sin before He admits him to the Garden. It is related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The exception in the two verses concerns the people of the Garden." Its meaning, as we have mentioned, is that there is no eternal abiding in the Fire for a Muslim sinner who enters the Fire, since he will come out of it, and there is likewise no eternal abiding for him in the Garden, because he did not enter the Garden at the outset. The Mu'tazilah, since they did not see the sinners coming out of the Fire, rejected the traditions reported on this subject, and sufficient is it as a manifest sin. ﴿A gift unbroken﴾: not cut off, but extending without end, like His saying ﴿for them is a reward unending﴾. It is in the accusative as an infinitive, meaning: they were given "a gift." It has been said: the Jahmiyyah disbelieved on account of four verses: ﴿A gift unbroken﴾; ﴿its fruit is constant﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35]; ﴿and what is with Allah is lasting﴾ [al-Nahl: 96]; ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 33].

When Allah related the accounts of the idol-worshippers and mentioned what vengeance He had brought upon them and what punishment He had prepared for them, He said: ﴿So do not be in doubt about what these worship﴾, meaning: do not be in doubt, after what has been revealed to you of these narratives, about the evil end of their worship, given what befell their like before them. This is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a promise of retribution against them, and a warning to them. Then He said: ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before them﴾. He means that their state in polytheism is like the state of their fathers, and you have been told what befell their fathers, so the like of it will befall them. This is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) whose meaning is to give the reason for the prohibition against doubt. The "mā" in "mimmā" and "kamā" is either a verbal-source particle (maṣdariyyah) or a relative pronoun (mawṣūlah): that is, "from their worship" and "like their worship," or "from what they worship of idols" and "like what they worship of them." ﴿And indeed We will give them their portion﴾: their share of punishment, just as We gave their fathers their portions. ﴿Without any diminution﴾: this is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) from "their portion," meaning complete.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 110:

﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾, meaning the Tawrat (Torah), ﴿but it was disputed about﴾. A people believed in it and a people disbelieved in it, just as the Qur'an was disputed about. This is a consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿Had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾, that He would not hasten their punishment, ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, between the people of Musa or your people, ﴿by a punishment that uproots﴾. ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt about it﴾, about the Qur'an or about the punishment (p. 87) ﴿disquieting﴾. From arabar-rajulu, when a man is one who has doubt (riyba), by way of figurative attribution (al-isnad al-majazi).

﴿And indeed, all [of them]﴾. The tanwin (nunation) is a substitute for the noun annexed to it (al-mudaf ilayh), meaning: and indeed all of them, that is, all of those who differ concerning it. "Inna" is read with a doubled nun. ﴿Lamma﴾ is read with a light (mukhaffaf) "mim" by the Basran and ‘Alī readers, with "mā" being superfluous (zā'idah). It was brought in to separate the lām of "inna" from the lām of ﴿la-yuwaffiyannahum﴾, which is the answer to an implied oath. The lām in "lamma" serves as a preparatory lām for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭi'ah). The meaning is: and indeed all of them, by Allah, your Lord will surely pay them in full ﴿their deeds﴾, that is, the recompense for their deeds, of faith and denial, of good and evil. Contrary to the first reading, Abū Bakr, and Makkī and Nāfi‘ read "inna" and "lamma" with light (mukhaffafatān), applying the light particle's function to that of the heavy one, considering its original form, which is the heavy form. Also, because "in" resembles the verb, and the verb governs both before and after its elision, as in ﴿lam yakun﴾ and ﴿lam yak﴾, so the thing it resembles is treated likewise. The others read both with doubled letters (mushaddadatān), and this is problematic. The best that has been said about it is that it derives from "lamamtu al-shay'" (I gathered the thing), meaning "jama'tuhu lamman" (I gathered it together). Then it was pausal (waqf), so it became "lammā," and then the connection was treated in the manner of pause. It may also be like "al-da'wā" and "al-tharwā" and the other verbal nouns that have the feminine alif (alif al-ta'nīth). Al-Zuhrī read "wa-inna kullan lammān" with tanwin, like His saying ﴿akulan lamman﴾ [al-Fajr: 19], and this supports what we have mentioned. The meaning is: and indeed all of them are gathered together, that is, brought together, as if it were said: and indeed all of them together, like His saying ﴿fa-sajada al-malā'ikatu kulluhum ajma‘ūn﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 30]. The author of al-Ijāz said: "lammā" in this has the sense of a temporal adverb (ẓarf), and an ellipsis has entered the speech, as if it were said: "wa-inna kullan lammā" [were gathered/brought] "la-yuwaffiyannahum rabbuka a‘mālahum." Al-Kisā'ī said: "I have no knowledge of the doubling of 'lammā'." ﴿Indeed He is Acquainted with what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 112:

﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾: be steadfast with a steadfastness like the steadfastness you were commanded with, not deviating from it. ﴿And those who have turned with you [in repentance]﴾: this is conjoined (ma'tuf) to the pronoun hidden in "istaqim" (be steadfast), and it is permissible because of the intervening separator (lil-fasil). That is: you be steadfast, and let those who have turned away from disbelief and returned to Allah sincerely also be steadfast. ﴿And do not transgress﴾: do not go beyond the limits of Allah. ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾: so He will recompense you, so fear Him. It is said: no verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that was harder on him than this verse, and for this reason he said, "Hud has made me grey."

**"And do not incline toward those who do wrong"** means: do not lean toward them. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This is addressed to the followers of the disbelievers, meaning: do not lean toward the leaders and the great ones in their wrongdoing and in what they call you to. **"Or the Fire will touch you."** It was also said that inclining toward them means being pleased with their disbelief. Qatadah said: "Do not join the polytheists." It is related from al-Muwaffaq that he prayed behind an imam, and when he recited this verse he fainted. When he came to, he was asked about it and said: "This is about one who inclines toward one who does wrong, so what of the wrongdoer himself?" It is related from al-Hasan: "Allah placed those between two negations: **'And do not transgress'** [Hud: 112] **'and do not incline.'"** Sufyan said: "In Hell there is a valley which none inhabits except the reciters who visit the kings." It is related from al-Awza'i: "There is nothing more hateful to Allah than a scholar who visits a ruler." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays for the long life of a wrongdoer has loved that Allah be disobeyed on His earth." Sufyan was asked about a wrongdoer who was on the verge of death in a desert, whether he should be given a sip of water. He said: "No." It was said to him: "He will die." He said: "Leave him to die." **"And you have no protectors apart from Allah"** is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to His words **"or the Fire will touch you"**, meaning: the Fire will touch you while you are in this state. Its meaning is: you have no protectors apart from Allah who are able to shield you from His punishment, and none other than Him is able to shield you from it. **"Then you will not be helped"**: then He will not help you, because He has decreed your punishment. The meaning of "then" (thumma) here is deeming it remote: help from Allah is remote.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 114:

﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, at dawn (ghadwa) and in the evening (ʿashiyya), ﴿and in the first hours of the night﴾. The word zulaf is the plural of zulfa, which means the hours of the night close to the end of the day. It comes from azlafahu, meaning "he brought it near." The prayer of ghadwa is the dawn prayer (al-Fajr). The prayer of ʿashiyya is the noon prayer (al-Zuhr) and the afternoon prayer (al-ʿAsr), because whatever comes after the decline of the sun (al-zawal) is ʿashiyy. The prayer of the zulaf is the sunset prayer (al-Maghrib) and the night prayer (al-ʿIsha larger). The accusative in ﴿طَرَفَيِ النَهارِ﴾ (ṭarafay al-nahar) is an adverb of time (ẓarf, an adverbial complement of time or place), because both words are annexed to a time-noun, as in your saying: "I stayed with him all of the day (jamīʿ al-nahār), I came to him at midday (niṣf al-nahār), at its beginning (awwalahu) and at its end (ākhirahu)." All of this is in the accusative by giving the annexed noun (al-muḍāf) the ruling of the noun it is annexed to (al-muḍāf ilayhi).

﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾: indeed the five prayers remove sins. In a hadith: "Indeed the five prayers expiate the sins that are between them." Or the meaning is acts of obedience in general. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it." Or the meaning is: "Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar."

﴿That﴾ refers to "so be steadfast (fa-istaqim)" and what follows it, or to the Qur'an. ﴿A reminder for those who remember﴾: an admonition for those who take heed.

It was revealed concerning ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyya al-Ansari, a date seller, who said to a woman: "There are better dates in the house." She entered, and he kissed her. He regretted it, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) grieving and weeping (ḥākiyan bākiyan), and this verse was revealed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did you pray the afternoon prayer with us?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is an expiation for you." It was asked: "Is it for him specifically?" He said: "No, it is for people in general."

Translation of the passage:

"And be patient" [Hud 11:115]: upon carrying out what you have been commanded and refraining from what you have been forbidden. Nothing of it is complete except by it. "Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers." He has brought together what encompasses all the commands and prohibitions, from His saying "So be steadfast" [Hud 11:112] to His saying "And be patient," and other good deeds besides.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 116:

﴿Why then were there not among the generations before you﴾ fahalla (why not) kana. It is placed for exhortation (taḥḍīḍ, urging) and is specific to the verb. ﴿people of remainder﴾ — people of excellence and goodness. He called excellence and nobility "remainder" (baqiyya), because a man keeps back of what he brings forth the best and most excellent part, so it became a proverbial example of nobility and excellence. It is said: "So-and-so is of the remainder of the people," meaning: of their choicest. From this is their saying: "In the corners are hidden treasures, and among men are remnants" (fī al-zawāyā khabāyā wa-fī al-rijāl baqāyā). ﴿who forbid corruption on the earth﴾ — he (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and his community are astonished that among the nations whose destruction God mentions in this surah there was no group of people of intellect and religion who forbade others from unbelief and sins. ﴿except a few of those whom We saved from among them﴾ — this is an exception of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but a few of those generations whom We saved forbade corruption, and the rest abandoned the forbidding. The "min" in ﴿of those whom We saved﴾ is for explanation (bayan), not for partition (tab'id), because salvation was for the forbidders alone, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong﴾ [al-A'raf: 165]. ﴿And those who did wrong followed﴾ — i.e., those who abandoned forbidding the reprehensible. This is a conjunction (ʿaṭf) upon an implied element, meaning: except a few of those among them who forbade corruption, and those who did wrong followed their desires; so it is a conjunction upon "forbade." ﴿what they were given luxury in﴾ — i.e., they followed what they had become accustomed to in luxury and indulgence, from love of leadership and wealth and seeking the means of pleasant living, and they rejected enjoining good and forbidding evil and cast it behind their backs. ﴿and they were criminals﴾ — a parenthetical clause (i'tiraḍ) and a judgment against them that they were a criminal people.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 117:

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.﴾ The lam (ل) here is for emphasizing the negation. ﴿Unjustly﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the subject (the agent, i.e., God): meaning, it is not valid for God to destroy the cities while being unjust to them. ﴿While their people are reformers﴾ — (this is) to declare His essence free of injustice (tanzīh). It was also said that the injustice (ẓulm) is shirk (associating partners with God), meaning: He does not destroy the cities because of the shirk of their people, while they are reformers in their dealings among themselves, not adding to their shirk another corruption.

﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community﴾, i.e., in agreement upon faith and acts of obedience by choice. But He did not will that. The Mu'tazilah (the rationalist theological school) said: it is a will of compulsion (qasr), and that would remove the test, so it is not permissible. ﴿And they will not cease to be differing﴾ over disbelief and faith. That is, but He willed that they would be differing, since He knew that they would choose that. (p-٩١)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 119:

﴿Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ — (These are) people whom Allah has preserved from disagreement, so they agreed upon the religion of truth without disagreeing about it. ﴿And for that He created them﴾ — i.e., and for what they are upon of disagreement. According to us, He created them for that which He knew they would come to, of disagreement or agreement, and He did not create them for other than that which He knew they would come to. Thus (it is stated) in "Sharh al-Ta'wilat" (Explanation of the Interpretations). ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ — and it is His saying to the angels: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾, because of His knowledge of the great number of those who choose falsehood.

﴿وَكُلا﴾ The tanwin (nunation) in it is a replacement (ʿiwaḍ) for the genitive noun that is added to (al-muḍāf ilayhi), as if it were said: *wa-kulla naba'in* (and every report). It is in the accusative, governed by His words ﴿We relate to you (نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ)﴾. His words ﴿of the reports of the messengers (مِن أنْباءِ الرُسُلِ)﴾ are an explanation (bayān) of *kullan*. His words ﴿that with which We strengthen your heart (ما نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ)﴾ are a substitute (badal) for *kullan*. ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth (وَجاءَكَ في هَذِهِ الحَقُّ)﴾: that is, in this surah, or in these related reports, there is that which is true. ﴿And an admonition and a reminder for the believers (وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ)﴾. The meaning of strengthening his heart is increasing his certainty (yaqīn), because the accumulation of proofs is more firmly settling for the heart.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 121:

﴿And say to those who do not believe﴾ from among the people of Makkah and others, ﴿Act according to your station﴾, that is, according to your state and your way upon which you are, ﴿indeed we are acting according to our station﴾.

ﷺ

﴿And wait﴾ for the calamities (al-dawa'ir) to befall us, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for them to descend upon you, similar to what God Most High has related of the vengeances that descended upon those like you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 123:

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Nothing hidden from Him is concealed of what takes place in them, so your deeds are not concealed from Him. ﴿And to Him the whole matter is returned.﴾ Their affair and your affair must certainly return to Him, so that He will take vengeance on them for you. "Yurja‘u" (is returned) is read by Nafi‘ and Hafs. ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him.﴾ For He is sufficient for you and your guardian. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ [al-An‘am: 132] With the "ta'" (ta‘malun, "you do") it is read by Madani, Shami and Hafs, meaning: you and they, by giving precedence to the addressee. It was said: this verse is the conclusion of the Torah. And in a hadith: "Whoever wishes to be the strongest of people, let him rely upon Allah, the Exalted."
